changed_files.why: Task-owned. Adds the bounded lifecycle the task asked for: a registry of process-opened handles, release_conn/open_connection_count/ close_all_connections, the request_connection provider, and a FastAPI lifespan that releases everything at shutdown. get_conn keeps its signature and thread-local semantics; set_conn is untouched. Two handler bodies (post_review, export_reviews) move onto the scoped provider with no change to any response.

Task-owned. Adds db.initialize (migrations once per database, under a lock, never cached on failure) and db.close (roll back an open transaction, then close; idempotent; reports a rollback failure). run_migrations itself is unchanged, so existing callers and the F002 fixture keep working.

Task-owned and NEW (created because the task names it). 17 acceptance and lifecycle tests tagged F007-AT01..AT05 plus the step-05 and step-07 cases. Disposable tmp_path stores only; the canonical store is never touched.

Durability fix. --out is now optional and defaults to docs/evidence/gates/<name>.json, which git tracks; a record path git would ignore is refused with exit 4 BEFORE the gate runs; the record gained durability, output_chars, output_truncated and output_log, and the complete output is written beside the record whenever the 2 KB tail truncates it. Record fields the receipts already read are unchanged; the existing refusals (exit 2 usage, exit 3 nothing ran) keep their meanings.

Durability contract: 8 new tests covering the versioned default, refusal of an ignored path, the failing-gate and never-ran negatives, record-shape compatibility, and truncated-vs-complete output. One existing test changed because the behaviour it asserted was inverted by this fix: omitting --out is now the supported default, so 'missing --out is a usage error' became 'a missing command is still a usage error' (exit 2).

produced_interfaces: osteopatch.db.initialize(conn, db_path=None) -> list[int] - migrations once per database per process, under _MIGRATION_LOCK

acceptance_tests.evidence: ALREADY HELD - verified and reused, not rebuilt. test_at01_concurrent_reads_produce_no_interface_error: 8 threads x 25 gallery+detail reads through the production get_conn(), released by a Barrier; failures == [] and exactly 8 distinct handles, one per thread. Before the change, the same measurement on the same shape gave 200 requests over 8 threads with 0 exceptions, and a mixed gallery/detail/save probe gave 210 operations per run with 0 exceptions. Over HTTP (section 11 rehearsal) 40 concurrent GET /v1/images across 4 threads produced errors == []. No sqlite3.InterfaceError anywhere.

ALREADY HELD at the database layer - verified and now regression-locked. test_at02_distinct_writes_at_revision_zero_create_exactly_one_event: 8 threads, 8 distinct idempotency keys, ALL submitting expected_revision=0 at the same barrier instant; observed 1 created, 7 repo.ConflictError, 0 unexpected exceptions, and the store shows revision_number=1 exactly once with 1 total event for that image. test_at02_same_idempotency_key_replays_instead_of_double_writing: the same key from 8 threads gave 1 created + 7 replays (created=false), all at revision 1, 1 row total. The pre-change stampede probe measured the same numbers (created=1 conflicts=7 revision1_rows=1), so the guarantee comes from UNIQUE (image_id, revision_number) and the narrow IntegrityError -> ConflictError path in repo.submit_review, which F007 did not need to change.

WAS MISSING - this is what F007 built. Before: a 200-request/8-thread probe left all 8 handles OPEN with nothing to close them, app.router.lifespan_context was Starlette's _DefaultLifespan (no shutdown hook), and a handler exception after a write left conn.in_transaction == True while an independent writer's BEGIN IMMEDIATE returned 'database is locked'. After: test_at03_release_rolls_back_and_closes_this_threads_connection (release rolls the uncommitted row back, closes the handle, hands the next request a fresh one, and an independent connection can take the write lock immediately); test_at03_release_is_idempotent_and_safe_when_nothing_is_open; test_at03_shutdown_closes_every_open_connection (4 threads hold 4 handles -> close_all_connections returns 4, count 0, all handles closed); test_at03_app_lifespan_shutdown_releases_connections (a real TestClient lifespan leaves open_connection_count() == 0); test_at03_handler_exception_leaves_no_transaction_for_the_next_request (RuntimeError propagates, handle closed, next scope starts with in_transaction False and can write); test_nested_request_scopes_release_once_at_the_outermost_exit.

ALREADY HELD and preserved. test_at04_injected_connection_survives_the_request_lifecycle: with app_module.set_conn(injected) and db.connect spied, a scoped request and real HTTP GET /v1/images + /v1/health both work, the injected handle is still open afterwards, open_connection_count() is 0, and the spy recorded zero opens - an injected fixture never touches a second store. test_at04_uninjected_requests_only_open_the_disposable_store: three uninjected HTTP requests recorded exactly one opened path, the per-test tmp_path database, and nothing else. The pre-existing conftest `client` fixture (set_conn + TestClient) and the whole 155-test G6 suite still pass unchanged.

ALREADY HELD for review errors; F007 added the release-path guarantee. test_at05_failed_write_inside_a_request_propagates_and_commits_nothing: a duplicate revision INSERT inside a scoped request raises sqlite3.IntegrityError OUT of the scope (the finally releases, it does not swallow) and the store still holds only the one good event. test_at05_review_conflicts_surface_as_failures_over_http: 201 created, then the same key replays 200 with created=false, a stale revision returns 409 with detail {expected_revision: 0, current_revision: 1}, an unknown image returns 404, and the review state afterwards is revision 1 / status reviewed / history length 1 - the conflict did not become a second saved review. db.close reports a rollback failure on stderr instead of hiding it (swept with a duck-typed connection whose rollback raises).

limitations: Read-only handlers still reuse their worker thread's handle, so open connections after traffic equal the number of distinct worker threads the server used (measured: 4 open after 40 concurrent HTTP reads across 4 threads). That is bounded by the thread pool and released at shutdown, which is the behavior F007 chose deliberately; converting every read to a per-request scope was left out to keep the change inside the task's boundary. An integrator who wants per-request reads can wrap the remaining handlers in request_connection() without further design work.

close_all_connections() closes handles another thread may still be using. Under Starlette the lifespan runs after in-flight requests drain, so this only matters for a manual call; measured behaviour is a loud ProgrammingError on the other thread, not a silent wrong answer.

db.initialize records a migrated database by resolved path. If the database FILE is replaced underneath a running process, the memo does not re-run migrations and the first query fails loudly with OperationalError: no such table: source_qc (swept). The pre-change code re-ran migrations per thread and would sometimes self-heal; that accident is gone by design.

The enterprise stack is untouched (task step 08). enterprise/app.py keeps its own module-level _conn with no lifespan, and enterprise/review_proxy.py reaches G6 reads through _g6().get_conn(), so in an enterprise-only process the G6 thread-local handles are still released by close_all_connections() rather than by that app's shutdown. That is recorded as separate later work, not silently changed here.

F007 did not touch F003's scope resolution, including the MODE_PROJECT_ONLY compatibility adapter, which remains a known narrower-scope path on a live code path and an integrator decision. F007's reads go through it unchanged.

No real-image, real-browser or real-data concurrency evidence was produced. The 10 skipped G6 tests (torch-gated bundle and browser attribution checks) remain SKIPPED, and a skipped real-asset check is not a real-asset pass.

A timeout or cancellation after a write is still reported by the existing optimistic-concurrency contract rather than reconciled by F007: a client that gets no answer must re-read the revision. F007 guarantees the outcome is not silently swallowed, not that it is automatically resolved.
